targetPath: /multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia/interests/adventure/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore Adventures in Brazil, Chile and Colombia"
lead: >-
  The adventurous side of an extensive journey through Brazil, Chile and Colombia includes nature walks at Iguazu, the high-altitude Atacama and a visit to El Peñon de Guatape. But the established itinerary covers eight countries, and its two-day off-road 4×4 section takes place in Bolivia. We explain which activities are included, which are offered separately and why this cannot be considered a trekking tour in each of the three selected countries.
---

## Brazil, Chile and Colombia: What “Adventure” Really Means

The current [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) includes [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), Iguazu Falls, Santiago and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), followed later by Medellin, [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/), Cartagena and Bogota. These stops offer memorable natural and urban experiences. However, **the adventure tag applies to the entire tour, not to a dedicated sporting itinerary in every selected country**.

The most substantial off-road section takes place **after Chile, in Bolivia**: two days by 4×4 through high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni. Between Brazil and Chile the route visits Argentina and Uruguay; between Chile and Colombia, it passes through Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. This is not a short direct Rio–Atacama–Colombia journey. The complete sequence is shown in the [general Brazil–Chile–Colombia selection](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia/).

When choosing a journey, distinguish **included excursions**, **optional activities** and **possible customized changes**. Each has its own cost, difficulty and time requirements.

## Brazil: Iguazu, Walking Routes and Macuco Safari

In [Rio](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the itinerary includes Corcovado with Christ the Redeemer and a visit to Sugarloaf Mountain. These city tours and viewpoints reveal the mountainous terrain and forested landscape using established tourist infrastructure. **Sporting treks through Tijuca Forest are not listed on this itinerary**, even though the national park has walking trails.

The country's principal natural highlight is [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). An excursion on the Brazilian side with a Russian-speaking guide is included. At the viewpoints, comfortable shoes, sun protection and preparation for spray are useful. This is a nature excursion with walking, not an arduous multi-day hike.

**Macuco Safari at Iguazu is offered only as an extra paid activity.** The excursion description includes forest and boat sections; the exact format and participation conditions should be confirmed before booking. The Bird Park is offered separately as well. Neither should automatically be counted among the paid inclusions of the main tour.

If adventure is your main objective, this is the place to decide whether an additional activity is desirable and whether it fits into an already busy day at the waterfalls.

## Chile: San Pedro de Atacama as Preparation for the Highland Stage

After [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the group flies to Calama and travels to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The stop is scheduled **for acclimatization before high-altitude Bolivia**. The following day begins a journey across Altiplano roads and trails, including sections above 4,000 meters.

An optional paid nighttime astronomy excursion with telescopes can be arranged in the Atacama. Its date depends on observation conditions and must be confirmed separately. It is not a substitute for trekking, climbing or an organized sporting hike.

The main question is altitude tolerance. Even when most of the onward trip is spent in a vehicle, rapid ascent can cause altitude sickness. Allow time for acclimatization, pack warm clothing and sun and wind protection, and consult a physician where health risks are present. Chile's national tourism portal also draws attention to the Atacama's cold nights and the need to dress for contrasting temperatures.

An unplanned strenuous hike should not be added before crossing into Bolivia merely to make the tour seem “more adventurous”: it could impair recovery before the expedition section already scheduled.

## Colombia: Guatape and City Excursions

A trip from [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/) to [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/) and [El Peñon de Guatape](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) is included. The itinerary describes an approximately eight-hour excursion with an English-speaking guide: a replica of the old El Peñol settlement, the rock, the town's painted facades and views of the reservoirs. Travel around Guatape by moto-taxi is planned.

**Visiting the rock and climbing its staircase are different activities.** A separate ascent of the steps cannot be confirmed as included in this excursion. Anyone wishing to reach the summit must check access, price, physical demands, available time and whether an ascent can be added to that day's program. It must not be presented as already paid for.

Other Colombian days include [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/), historic [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/) and Zipaquira. These are busy journeys and walks, but their central attractions are culture, architecture and history rather than extreme sports. After an extensive journey, accumulated fatigue from flights and excursions matters even if each day's individual exertion is moderate.

## Where the Main Physical Challenge Lies

| Stage | Actual demands |
|---|---|
| Rio and Iguazu | Walking, stairs and viewpoints |
| Atacama, followed by Bolivia | Altitude, cold and 4×4 roads |
| Guatape and Colombian cities | Long excursions and walking |

This trip is better suited to travelers who want **to combine several types of experience** than to those seeking continuous sporting challenges. Independent mountaineering, multi-day trekking, rafting and specialist equipment are not promised. For those activities, choose a program describing each sporting stage separately, including duration, difficulty and participation conditions.

The climate changes substantially too: humid Brazil, a dry highland stage with cold nights, followed by Colombia's varied temperatures and elevations. Layered clothing, comfortable footwear, sun protection and a small daypack are useful. Confirm checked-baggage allowances and restrictions on domestic flights before departure, especially when taking personal sporting equipment.

Ada Tours can discuss adding a specific adventure and which other stops would need to be shortened as a result. Such an addition is assessed against the itinerary, weather constraints, transport schedule and cost; it is not included automatically.

Other options are available in the [adventure tours catalog](/interests/adventure/) and [multi-country adventure journeys](/multi-country/interests/adventure/). You can also compare [adventure routes featuring Chile](/interests/adventure/tours/chile/).

## Frequently Asked Questions About Adventure in Brazil, Chile and Colombia

### Is there a sporting trek in all three countries?

No. The current tour combines urban sightseeing and nature excursions. Its most substantial 4×4 off-road activity takes place in Bolivia, which is also on the longer route.

### Is Macuco Safari included in the tour price?

No. Macuco Safari at Iguazu is offered separately at an additional charge. The basic guided excursion on the Brazilian side of the falls is a different included activity.

### Why is travel through the Atacama considered an adventure?

The Atacama serves as preparation for the high-altitude journey across Bolivia. The scheduled San Pedro de Atacama stop includes the transfer and acclimatization; the astronomy excursion is optional.

### Can I climb El Peñon de Guatape?

The route includes a visit to the area around the rock, but climbing the staircase is not explicitly listed as a paid inclusion. Its availability, time requirements and physical demands must be agreed separately.

kind: multi_country_interest

buttonLabel: "Cultural Route: Brazil, Chile and Colombia"
lead: >-
  On an extended journey through South America, three countries tell very different cultural stories: Rio de Janeiro and its urban landmarks, the historic center of Santiago, colonial Cartagena, Medellin's art and Bogota's museums. We explain what is actually included, how the days are distributed and which parts of the journey focus mainly on nature.
---

## What Connects the Cultures of Brazil, Chile and Colombia?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: [“Eight South American Countries in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). It is **an eight-country itinerary**, not an independent trip only to Brazil, Chile and Colombia. Selecting these three lets you follow one cultural thread through the larger journey, from [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) via [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) to Colombia's cities.

These stages offer different experiences. Brazil introduces Rio's city panoramas, the religious landmark of Corcovado and urban architecture. Chile features historic and contemporary Santiago. Colombia receives more time: [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/), [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/), [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/) and Zipaquira. Between these stages lie Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador, so **there is no direct three-country connection** and travelers should not expect a continuous “cultural tour of three capitals.”

For all programs with this geographical combination, without the theme filter, visit the [Brazil–Chile–Colombia catalog](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia/). Here we focus on the historical and cultural components.

## Brazil: Rio, Religious Landmarks and Urban Architecture

The journey begins with an arrival in Sao Paulo, but the first day is devoted to a transfer and rest, followed by a flight to Rio the next day. **There is no full cultural tour of Sao Paulo** scheduled for these days. Rio is the main Brazilian city destination.

On day three, a group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide visits Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer. Day four features Sugarloaf Mountain and a city tour, including the [Cathedral of Saint Sebastian](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Together these experiences introduce urban history, architecture and contemporary Brazilian landmarks, while natural panoramas provide the setting for exploring Rio itself.

After Rio, the group flies to [Foz do Iguacu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and walks along the Brazilian side of the waterfalls. **Iguazu is primarily a nature stage**, even when the overall tour appears in the “Culture and History” selection. Visits to the Bird Park and Macuco Safari can be added at extra cost, but they are not components of the included cultural excursion. Compare other [culture and history tours in Brazil](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/).

## Chile: Historic Santiago and a Short Transition to the Atacama

After the Argentine and Uruguayan stages, the itinerary includes a flight to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). A group city tour with a Russian-speaking guide takes place the following day. The description includes Plaza de Armas, the cathedral, La Moneda Palace and other buildings of the historic center.

Santiago's historic square brings together buildings associated with colonial administration, later urban development and the independent republic. La Moneda Palace belongs to another period of Chilean political history. These sights fit well into a city excursion, but entry to every building cannot be promised: the confirmed service is **a general sightseeing tour**, not a set of tickets to all museums.

The itinerary then continues through Calama to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) to prepare for the Bolivian crossing. A nighttime astronomy excursion can be added separately, as can a wine tour in the Maipo Valley. Neither optional activity should be presented as part of Chile's compulsory cultural program.

Chile's cultural contribution to this long trip is therefore concentrated in Santiago. To explore Chilean museums or the architecture of other cities in depth, compare [other culture and history tours in Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/).

## Colombia: From Comuna 13 to Cartagena's Fortresses

The Colombian leg is the most varied in urban subject matter. After flying from Guayaquil, the group arrives in [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/). A trip to [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñon Rock is planned, followed by a sightseeing excursion around Medellin and [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/). Its cultural value comes partly from the modern city: public spaces, street art and the history of neighborhood transformation. The separate [Medellin and Comuna 13 excursion](/colombia/medellin/medellin-city-and-comuna-13/) describes this experience.

The next stop is [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). Its fortified historic center is linked to trade, defense of a Caribbean port and colonial history. The city walls and fortifications form a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The program lists historic streets, the Church of San Pedro Claver, squares and a panoramic look at San Felipe de Barajas Fortress. An important distinction: a panoramic view does not automatically mean entering every fortification or museum.

The final cultural days are in [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/). The city program mentions historic La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Mint, the Botero collection and Plaza Bolivar. The day ends with an ascent to Monserrate. Then comes an [excursion to the Salt Cathedral of Zipaquira](/colombia/zipaquira/zipaquira-salt-cathedral-5-hours/), offering an introduction to a modern religious space created in former salt workings.

Colombia thus spans several eras and forms of cultural life: colonial port heritage, historic capital districts, museum collections and contemporary urban art. This gives the Colombian stage a different emphasis from the shorter city visits in Rio and Santiago. Other possibilities appear in [Colombia's culture and history tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/).

## What to Consider When Planning Cultural Visits

Museum and historic-center programs have their own logistical constraints. In Bogota, the Gold Museum is normally closed on Mondays; other museum spaces associated with the Bank of the Republic operate on separate schedules. As a result, **the day of the week** affects whether all listed visits can take place, and sightseeing order may need to change. Check opening hours for the planned dates rather than relying on a generic list of attractions.

In Santiago and Cartagena, distinguish sightseeing, exterior views and entry to a particular museum. Visiting a square does not mean entering every building around it. Each site may have restrictions even when its historic neighborhood is open for walking.

The sequence of cities also matters: Rio and Iguazu are followed by Buenos Aires and Montevideo, then Santiago and the high-altitude route through Bolivia and Peru, while Colombia is reached via Ecuador. A short trip with “Rio–Santiago–Bogota” tickets cannot simply be imposed on this itinerary. An independent cultural route across the three countries would require different flights and a new allocation of days.

## What Cultural Experience Does the Full Program Offer?

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The tour combines Russian- and English-language excursions, organized transfers, domestic flights and 4-star hotels under its stated terms. Included experiences feature city tours in Rio, Santiago and Colombian cities. Other activities are offered separately, including an astronomy evening in the Atacama and tastings in the Maipo Valley.

If the main goal is **to compare the urban histories of three countries**, the sequence is rewarding: Rio's religious landmarks and landscape, Santiago's public spaces, Cartagena's colonial architecture and Bogota's museum collections. But this cultural narrative occupies only part of 32 days. Significant sections of the wider journey focus on waterfalls, highlands, archaeological sites in other countries and the Galapagos.

Ada Tours helps align museum visits with opening hours, coordinate connections between countries and clarify which stops include admission and which are panoramic. A shorter cultural trip can be discussed as a customized itinerary with a separate offer; the original tour's services should not be assumed to carry over automatically.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Brazil–Chile–Colombia Cultural Route

### Is a complete Sao Paulo sightseeing excursion included?

On the 32-day tour, Sao Paulo is an arrival point and a connection for an onward flight. Brazil's main cultural program takes place in Rio de Janeiro.

### Is the Atacama part of the included cultural excursion in Chile?

Following the Santiago city tour, the itinerary travels via Calama to San Pedro de Atacama. The astronomy evening and wine excursion are optional, not compulsory included activities.

### Which Colombian cities offer the most historical content?

On the established itinerary, Cartagena has a fortified colonial center, while Bogota has historic neighborhoods and museums. Medellin adds modern urban history and Comuna 13. All three cities reveal different sides of the country.

targetPath: /multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia/interests/nature/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Nature in Brazil, Chile and Colombia"
lead: >-
  The Brazilian part of the longer journey includes Iguazu Falls and Rio's green mountains; Chile features San Pedro de Atacama before the high-altitude crossing, and Colombia includes El Peñon Rock and Guatape. We describe the actual nature stops without confusing them with cultural excursions.
---

## Nature in Brazil, Chile and Colombia: Waterfalls, Desert and Green Mountains

Natural attractions differ dramatically on a journey through Brazil, Chile and Colombia. In Brazil, travelers see Rio de Janeiro's green slopes and [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). In Chile, our longer itinerary includes Santiago and [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/), the starting point for the onward journey to Bolivia's lagoons. In Colombia, the principal nature excursion is to [El Peñon Rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/).

This combination is part of Ada Tours' [32-day itinerary through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Brazil comes at the beginning, Chile after Argentina and Uruguay, and Colombia at the end following Peru and Ecuador. This page therefore does not describe direct flights between three consecutive countries or a stand-alone three-country expedition.

## What to See in Brazil: A Forested City and Major Waterfalls

In Rio, the program includes Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer, reached through the forested [Tijuca](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/) area, along with Sugarloaf Mountain and panoramic viewpoints. This is primarily a visit to a vast city set among coastal mountains and greenery. It does not imply a separate multi-day trek through the Atlantic Forest or sightings of rare animals.

The group then flies to Foz do Iguacu. The itinerary includes an excursion to the waterfalls on the Brazilian side, followed the next day by a visit to the Argentine side. These are different national parks across an international border, even though the waterfall system is one. Travelers see the cascades from different angles; a high water level or a rainbow on any particular day cannot be guaranteed.

**The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are optional paid activities.** They should not be assumed to be part of the basic nature program simply because they are nearby. The key experiences are the included excursions on both sides of Iguazu and the time allowed for walking.

## Chile: The Atacama as a Gateway to the Highlands

After Santiago, the tour flies to Calama and transfers to San Pedro de Atacama. This stop is included partly for acclimatization ahead of the Bolivian 4×4 stage. An optional evening astronomy excursion with telescopes is available separately.

This is an essential distinction from tours devoted entirely to Chile. **Extensive exploration of every major Atacama attraction, a trip to Patagonia or a visit to Torres del Paine are not included.** From San Pedro, travelers head toward the Bolivian border; the colorful lagoons, geothermal areas and Uyuni Salt Flat visited afterwards lie in Bolivia. When selecting a nature journey, these should not be incorrectly assigned to the Chilean day.

If you want Chilean glaciers or walking trails in particular, compare [other nature trips combining Brazil and Chile](/multi-country/brazil_chile/interests/nature/). The same two countries can feature very different natural regions on different itineraries.

## Colombia: Guatape Is the Main Nature Highlight

The Colombian stage begins in Medellin. A day is allocated to El Peñol, the monolithic [El Peñon de Guatape](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and colorful [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/). Views over the winding reservoir and green shorelines contrast strongly with the dry landscapes seen several days earlier on the Altiplano. The excursion is described as eight hours with an English-speaking guide.

Separate Colombian days cover Medellin and Comuna 13, Cartagena, Bogota and a trip to Zipaquira. Each has its own appeal, but city excursions do not become trekking or nature safaris because the complete tour has a “Nature” interest tag. In Bogota, Monserrate offers a panorama of the capital; it is not an independent expedition to a national park.

**The Amazon and specialized multi-day wildlife-watching excursions in Colombia are not part of the confirmed route.** Travelers wishing to spend more time in forests, watching birds or walking in mountains should compare actual daily schedules rather than country names alone.

| Stage | Main natural scene |
|---|---|
| Rio | Tijuca and the coastal mountains |
| Iguazu | Cascades on both sides of the border |
| Northern Chile | San Pedro's desert landscape |
| Colombia | Guatape rock and reservoir |

## Weather and Pace: Three Different Sets of Conditions

Rio and Iguazu can be hot and very humid, so protection from spray is needed at the waterfalls. Around San Pedro the air is drier, sunshine stronger and nights cooler; immediately afterwards the Bolivian high-altitude stage begins. In Colombia, the climate changes considerably between mountainous Medellin, Caribbean Cartagena and higher-elevation Bogota.

The same shoes and clothes are not suitable for every stop. Take lightweight tropical clothing, closed-toe shoes, wind and rain protection and warm layers for the highlands. Keeping documents and essentials in a separate bag is useful on a journey with so many flights.

These contrasts also affect planning physical exertion. Iguazu is explored mainly on equipped walking paths. San Pedro is a relatively short stop, followed by elevations over 4,000 meters. A considerable part of the Guatape excursion is spent on the road from Medellin. The number of countries alone says little about the intensity of the trip.

## Entry Rules and Payments: Check All Eight Countries

For a traveler with a Russian international passport, Brazil and Colombia have their own short-stay entry rules, while Chile's procedures must be checked separately. But the complete tour also visits Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. Checking the three countries in the title is not enough, particularly around the crossing to the Argentine side of Iguazu.

Brazil uses the real, Chile the peso and Colombia the Colombian peso. Flights between countries and different bank-card acceptance rules make it useful to agree in advance how services will be paid and to hold permitted cash for personal expenses. A dollar-denominated tour price does not establish whether a particular bank card works abroad.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Frequently Asked Questions About Nature in Brazil, Chile and Colombia

### Does the Chilean section include Patagonia?

No. On the confirmed long tour, Chile is represented by Santiago, Calama and San Pedro de Atacama. Travelers cross into Bolivia afterwards. A trip to Chilean Patagonia would require a different itinerary.

### Is there a wildlife safari in Colombia?

On this tour, Colombia's nature experience centers on Guatape and El Peñon Rock. There is no specialist safari or Amazon expedition. Choose this tour for its actual mix of natural scenery and city experiences.

### Are both sides of Iguazu Falls included?

Yes. The confirmed itinerary includes separate excursion days for the Brazilian and Argentine sides. Additional activities in the waterfall area must be distinguished from these included visits.

targetPath: /multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia/interests/wildlife/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Where to Watch Wildlife on a Trip Through Brazil, Chile and Colombia"
lead: >-
  Wildlife experiences on a route through Brazil, Chile and Colombia are distributed unevenly. Brazil includes Iguazu Falls and the Atlantic Forest, Chile features the dry northern Atacama, while the Colombian days focus mainly on cities and mountain panoramas. Scheduled marine wildlife observation occurs in the Galapagos of Ecuador, outside the selected three countries. We explain where the itinerary offers landscapes and where actual encounters with wildlife are planned.
---

## Wildlife and Safari: What's Included on a Brazil–Chile–Colombia Route

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Brazil, Chile and Colombia as main countries on the route and “Wildlife and Safari” as a theme supported by the nature-observation program. For example, the [journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) combines Iguazu, Atacama, the Andean highlands, the Galapagos and the Caribbean coast. **This is not a three-country tour:** between Brazil, Chile and Colombia, the itinerary also passes through Argentina, Uruguay, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador.

When choosing a trip to see animals, distinguish three experiences: walking through natural scenery, visiting a protected area and dedicated wildlife watching. Each offers something different. A theme name alone does not mean every day is devoted to ornithology or photographic safaris.

| Country | What travelers see |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Iguazu Falls and the Atlantic Forest |
| Chile | Atacama Desert, beginning of the high-altitude stage |
| Colombia | Green mountains around Guatape and urban scenery |

For comparison of terms and the complete geography, visit the [Brazil, Chile and Colombia tour selection](/multi-country/brazil_chile_colombia/). It shows itineraries that include these countries even when other countries lie between them.

## Brazil: Iguazu Falls and Opportunities to Observe Wildlife

The first days of the longer journey are spent in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain offer views of the bay, ocean and green hills. [Tijuca National Park](/brazil/place/tijuca-national-park/) covers parts of the slopes. However, the included Rio excursions mainly focus on urban sightseeing and famous viewpoints, not dedicated observation of rare animals.

Brazil's key nature stage is [Foz do Iguacu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The national park protects a substantial area of Atlantic Forest. UNESCO notes its valuable habitats for rare species, including jaguars and giant otters. Their presence in a protected area, however, is no guarantee of meeting one during an ordinary tourist visit.

The included program explores the Brazilian side of the waterfalls, followed by the Argentine side. Near Foz do Iguacu, an additional visit to the Bird Park is available; the Macuco Safari boat trip is also optional. **Distinguish the included waterfall excursion from activities charged separately**. A boat ride does not amount to a safari for large animals, and the Bird Park is a different experience.

If seeing animals is your principal reason for traveling, compare [wildlife-watching tours in Brazil](/interests/wildlife/tours/brazil/). The Amazon and Pantanal are not part of this itinerary merely because it includes Brazil.

## Chile: Atacama and the Transition to the Highlands

Travelers fly from Argentina to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), explore the city, then fly to Calama and travel to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The desert changes the conditions of travel: dry air, strong daytime sun, cool nights and the need to acclimatize before climbing higher.

An optional astronomy excursion with telescopes is available on the Chilean stage. A separate birdwatching trip to protected Chilean lagoons **is not included in the compulsory program**. This distinction matters: beautiful photographs of flamingos in the Atacama do not mean a birdwatching excursion is included.

From San Pedro, the route crosses the Bolivian border. It is **on Bolivian territory** that the off-road days visit Laguna Verde, Laguna Colorada and other highland lakes, followed by the Uyuni Salt Flat. These nature stops belong to the wider journey but must not be described as excursions within Chile.

Travelers attracted by high-altitude landscapes should compare elevation, drive duration and acclimatization pace. There is no lengthy trekking route through Chile's mountains in this itinerary.

## Colombia: Green Andes, Guatape and Cities

Colombia's stage begins in [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/). A trip to [Guatape](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñon Rock is planned, offering views of mountains, valleys and the reservoir. The route then continues through [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/) and [Zipaquira](/colombia/place/zipaquira/).

Colombia has diverse wildlife, but **this particular stage of the eight-country tour is primarily cultural and urban**. There is no separately organized wildlife-watching excursion to a national park on the Colombian part of the itinerary. Guatape offers landscapes, Cartagena the Caribbean coast and architecture, and Bogota the historic center, museums and mountain panoramas. These are different reasons to travel, but none guarantees bird or mammal sightings.

Anyone particularly interested in Colombian wildlife should start with [Colombia's tour catalog](/colombia/tour/) and look for dedicated nature days in the actual schedules. Ada Tours can help discuss priorities, but the content of another excursion cannot be transferred into the approved itinerary without separate confirmation.

## Why the Most Substantial Wildlife Experience Takes Place in Ecuador

On the same [32-day journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), Ecuador comes after Peru. Travelers leave Quito for the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The archipelago is known for endemic species and a rich marine environment.

On [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), the program includes the highlands and lava tunnels. A later day offers **one of two marine itineraries**, chosen when booking is confirmed: [North Seymour Island](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and Bachas beaches or [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) with Cape Carrion. Depending on the route, travelers may see seabirds, iguanas and sea lions; swimming and snorkeling conditions differ as well.

These are **alternatives for a single day**, not two included excursions in succession. Even in areas where animals are frequently seen, a particular species, number of sightings and weather conditions cannot be guaranteed. Ada Tours helps compare the island days, time restrictions, confirmed excursion and onward flights.

Useful comparisons include [wildlife-watching tours in Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/) and the [Brazil, Chile and Ecuador selection](/multi-country/brazil_chile_ecuador/interests/wildlife/). These filters can also include other countries.

## Climate, Documents and Pace: Connecting Three Countries on One Journey

Humid Iguazu, Chile's dry north, Bolivia's highlands, Ecuador's island ecosystem and Colombia's warm Caribbean coast call for different equipment. At the falls, take a waterproof outer layer and closed shoes; in the desert, sun protection and evening insulation; on the islands, lightweight clothes and protection against sea spray. Gradual ascent and personal tolerance of exertion are especially important on high-altitude sections.

International flights and the overland Chile–Bolivia crossing require separate documentation checks. Visas, re-entry permissions, transit rules and medical requirements depend on nationality and travel date; no single set of requirements can be assumed for all passengers. Likewise, check payment methods and the acceptance of particular bank cards in each country, rather than assuming identical access throughout the continent.

When organizing the longer tour, we help plan flights and ground transfers, check documents for the client's citizenship, coordinate hotels and guides, and allow reasonable connection time. For travelers especially interested in animals, the most useful criterion is **how many days are actually dedicated to wildlife watching**, rather than how many natural sites are mentioned.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Wildlife Watching in Brazil, Chile and Colombia

### Does this catalog include a tour only to the selected three countries?

The 32-day itinerary considered here passes through eight main countries. A trip only through Brazil, Chile and Colombia would need a separately agreed route and confirmation of availability.

### Could I see a jaguar on the Iguazu excursion?

Jaguars live in the national park's forest, but a standard waterfall excursion does not include guaranteed sightings of rare predators.

### Is a visit to Chilean flamingo lagoons included?

On this tour, Chile is represented by Santiago and Atacama. The high-altitude lagoons visited on the subsequent 4×4 journey are in Bolivia; no compulsory specialist Chilean flamingo excursion is listed.

### Are both North Seymour and South Plaza visited?

No. They are alternatives for the Galapagos sea-excursion day. The actual option is confirmed at booking.

### Will there be a photographic safari in Colombia?

The current program covers cities and Guatape. No separate Colombian wildlife-watching excursion is included.

### How should I prepare for altitude when my goal is nature travel?

The Chilean stage leads into high-altitude travel in Bolivia and then Peru. Check the elevations and itinerary pace against personal health, and discuss exertion with a physician before departure if necessary.

## Four Countries, Four Very Different Stages of One Itinerary

This selection offers {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. It is the [“Eight South American Countries in 32 Days” tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/): the journey passes through Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. The four countries in this page's title are part of the main route, but **there is no separate tour in this selection limited to Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Ecuador**.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

These four countries offer a remarkable contrast. [Brazil](/brazil/) contributes the Atlantic coast, Rio's mountain panoramas and waterfalls. [Chile](/chile/) takes the journey into the arid Atacama and toward the high-altitude border. [Ecuador](/ecuador/) combines an Andean capital with protected island ecosystems. [Colombia](/colombia/) closes the trip with major cities, colonial Cartagena and the Caribbean coast.

The main practical issue is **how much time separates the stops that interest you**. Bolivia and Peru lie between Chile's Atacama and Ecuador's Quito on the actual itinerary, rather than a direct flight. Choosing this tour on the basis of four country names alone would be misleading: every intermediate day counts toward the journey's duration and physical demands.

## Brazil: From Rio's Panoramas to Both Sides of Iguazu

The journey starts in Sao Paulo, followed by a flight to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Included excursions visit Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and other city stops. Several days are spent among ocean bays, forested slopes and the distances of a large city.

Next comes [Foz do Iguacu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). First travelers see the Brazilian side of the waterfalls, then the Argentine side, after which they fly to Buenos Aires. Thus another country and an international border already feature in the opening Brazil-related part of the itinerary. The Bird Park and Macuco Safari are separately paid options; they should not be added automatically to the compulsory excursions.

After Argentina and a one-day stop in Uruguay, the Chilean portion begins. Brazil and Chile are linked by the complete route, but the full sightseeing stages between them must be included in calculations of flights and duration.

## Chile: Santiago, a Flight to Calama and the Start of the Highland Crossing

A group sightseeing excursion with a Russian-speaking guide is planned in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The next flight goes to Calama, followed by an overland transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). A stop here precedes the two-day off-road journey through Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons.

The transition from Santiago to the Atacama brings major changes in natural conditions. After humid Iguazu and large cities, travelers encounter dry air, significant daily temperature swings and highland environments. The journey calls for warm layers, sun protection and attention to altitude tolerance in advance. Discuss health concerns before departure, not only after crossing the Bolivian border.

On this itinerary, Chile **does not lead directly to Ecuador**. From the Atacama, travelers cross Bolivia, the Uyuni Salt Flat and La Paz, followed by Peru with Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu. Only after Lima is a flight to Quito scheduled. This is the defining feature of this country combination: an extensive historical and high-altitude section separates Chile's arid desert from Galapagos nature.

## Ecuador: Quito and Several Different Types of Island Day

In [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/), the itinerary includes a city tour and sites around the equator line. The journey then continues by air to the [Galapagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). The route includes Baltra, [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), the island highlands and Puerto Ayora.

This stage has a particular feature: **the actual marine route must be confirmed**. One excursion is included: either North Seymour and Bachas beaches or South Plaza and Cape Carrion. Both options together are not guaranteed. Travelers hoping to see particular bird species or other island wildlife should clarify the chosen marine program before booking.

The Galapagos require additional preparation for documents and baggage. Official rules include a TCT Transit Control Card and a biosecurity check of belongings before the flight from the mainland. Allow time for these procedures beyond ordinary airport check-in. The return to mainland Ecuador is via Guayaquil, with the next flight continuing to Colombia.

## Colombia: After the Islands, Medellin, Cartagena and Bogota

The Colombian stage begins in [Medellin](/colombia/place/medellin/). The program includes a visit to El Peñol and Guatape, a city excursion and Comuna 13. Next comes a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), where historic streets, the fortress and maritime atmosphere provide a striking contrast with the Andean highlands and Galapagos experiences.

The journey finishes in [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/), with the historic center, cultural attractions, Monserrate and a trip to Zipaquira's Salt Cathedral. This is not one long “rest period in Colombia,” but several separate urban stages connected by domestic flights and taking place at different elevations. The Guatape excursion has an English-speaking guide; Russian-speaking guides are provided for some city excursions. Check the language for each day rather than assuming it remains the same throughout.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Ecuador

### Can I fly straight from Chile to the Galapagos on this itinerary?

No. After the Atacama, the published tour goes through Bolivia and Peru. The flight to Quito comes only from Lima, followed by a flight to the Galapagos. A direct connection would need a different itinerary.

### Which country comes last?

[Colombia](/colombia/) is last. From Guayaquil, travelers visit Medellin, Cartagena and Bogota; the final flight is connected with Sao Paulo.

### Is the Bird Park at Iguazu included in the price?

No. It is an optional visit. The main waterfall excursions are described separately, and their exact inclusions appear on the [full tour page](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

### Can I choose a particular Galapagos island in advance?

You can discuss your preference before booking, but the included sea excursion follows one of two alternatives; the actual option must be confirmed.
